plan.summary: This 4-week block starts the 12-week off-camp build for boxing with one focused full-body S&C session each week. Week 1 establishes training maxes for the main lift so later percentage work is grounded in your current level, and the main build starts in Week 2. With only one weekly lift slot and a preference for more conditioning, the session keeps power and strength first, then adds practical upper-back, trunk, and short conditioning work without creating unnecessary fatigue.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build general lower-body strength, simple full-body power, and base conditioning with beginner-friendly exercise choices.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress strength and power with slightly heavier work while keeping the weekly session compact and recoverable.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Shift more toward fast, crisp power and speed expression while holding onto the strength built earlier.

exercises.name: Box Jump
exercises.notes: Use a box height that lets you land quietly and stable. Reset between reps and stay explosive.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if box setup is awkward. Jump as high as you can and stick the landing.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump

exercises.name: Back Squat
exercises.notes: Warm up in small jumps, then work up to one hard set of 3-5 reps with clean form. This sets your baseline for future percentage work.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then work up to your heaviest clean set of 3-5 reps. Log the load and reps so the app can estimate your training max.

substitutionOptions.name: Goblet Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this only if barbell squat setup is not practical. Still work up to one hard clean set of 3-5 reps.

exercises.notes: Drive elbows back and pause briefly at the top. Keep your chest planted on the pad and stop with 2 reps in reserve.

substitutionOptions.name: Seated Cable Row

substitutionOptions.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row

exercises.name: Bike Intervals
